page_title: Create A Real Time Chat App With Golang, Angular, And Websockets

sources.entry: Create a Real Time Chat App with Golang, Angular 2, and WebSocket

summary.title: Create A Real Time Chat App With Golang, Angular, And Websockets
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a real-time chat app with a Go websocket server (gorilla/websocket) and an Angular 2 client that talks to it over JavaScript WebSockets.
takeaways: How to upgrade HTTP requests to websockets in Go using the gorilla websocket library and accept cross-origin requests with CheckOrigin.
How to structure a Go chat server with a client manager goroutine plus per-client read and write goroutines communicating over channels.
How to wrap a browser WebSocket in an Angular service that emits open, close and message events.
How to bind messages to an Angular template and render system messages (prefixed with a slash) in bold.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a single-page chat application with a Golang server and an Angular 2 client. The Go server uses the gorilla websocket library and a satori UUID per client, with a ClientManager that tracks clients and broadcasts JSON messages across goroutines and channels. The Angular side uses the Angular CLI to create a SocketService that wraps the browser WebSocket API and an AppComponent that displays messages. The author notes the code partly borrows from other examples and does not store chat history.
